name.en: Election scams: fake PACs, “investment pools” and voter-registration texts

how.en: Around elections, scammers use candidates’ names, images and slogans, sometimes with AI-generated voices. They ask for donations to fake political action committees, sell campaign merchandise that never ships, or promise a guaranteed return on a “campaign pool” that pays out if the candidate wins. Others text or email that you are not registered to vote, with a link to a fake registration page that steals your personal information.

text.en: A message uses a candidate’s name, image or slogan.
It asks for a donation, sells merchandise, or offers a guaranteed return on a campaign pool.
Or it says you aren’t registered to vote and links to a page.
Your money or personal details go to the scammers.
ALERT: Our records show you are NOT registered to vote in your state. Confirm your registration before the deadline: [link]

en: A text saying you aren’t registered to vote, with a link.
Campaign donations described as an investment with returns.
Pressure to donate or recruit others.
Check your registration on your state’s official election website, typed yourself.
Campaign donations are never an investment.
Check committees on the Federal Election Commission website before giving.
